lessons.correction: Strengthen your ground army and increase technology investment. Consider adding air units for flexibility. Maintain expansion and production.
lessons.mistake: Continuing to expand and tech without reinforcing your army, assuming the enemy is passive.
lessons.recheck: Re-evaluate if the opponent transitions to heavy air or if you face a timing attack.
lessons.title: Ground vs Ground: Don't Overextend Economy
lessons.when: Early-midgame, both sides ground-oriented with heavy production and tech, around 300 seconds.
lessons.why: The opponent is ground-oriented, so a strong ground army is essential. Air units provide flexibility against potential air transitions.

lessons.correction: Focus on developing economy and technology while maintaining a light defensive posture. Use your Reaper for scouting to gather information.
lessons.mistake: Over-committing to tech at the expense of army production and neglecting scouting.
lessons.recheck: Re-evaluate when you have more scouting information or if the opponent shows signs of an early attack.
lessons.title: Early Game: Don't Overcommit to Tech
lessons.when: Early game, both sides unknown compositions, heavy economy and tech investment, around 180 seconds.
lessons.why: This sets up a strong midgame, and scouting helps you adapt to the opponent's choices.

lessons.correction: Add anti-air units such as Marines, Thors, or Vikings to counter the opponent's air presence. Maintain your ground army and continue expanding.
lessons.mistake: Neglecting your ground army entirely or over-investing in anti-air without a clear threat.
lessons.recheck: Re-evaluate if the opponent transitions back to ground or if you face a large push.
lessons.title: Ground vs Air: Don't Ignore Anti-Air
lessons.when: Early-midgame, opponent air-oriented with Phoenixes and Oracles, you have ground army with Siege Tanks and Marines, around 360 seconds.
lessons.why: The opponent's air units can be a threat, so you need a response. Adding anti-air units helps defend against harass and potential air attacks.
